chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to me from Sa'd ibn Abdillah, from Muhammad ibn Hammad, from his brother Ahmad ibn Hammad, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah, from his father, from his father, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) say: Jabra'il (peace be upon him) came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said to him, 'Peace be upon you, O Muhammad! Shall I give you glad tidings of a son whom your nation will kill after you?' He said, 'I do not need such a son.' He ascended to the heaven, then returned to him for the second time and said to him the same thing. He said, 'I do not need such a son.' He ascended to the heaven, then descended to him for the third time and said the same thing. He said, 'I do not need such a son.' He said, 'Verily your Lord is placing the succession in his progeny.' He said, 'Yes,' or he said that. Then the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) rose and entered upon Fatimah (peace be upon her) and said to her, 'Verily Jabra'il (peace be upon him) came to me and gave me glad tidings of a son whom my nation will kill after me.' She said, 'I do not need such a son.' He said to her, 'Verily my Lord is placing the succession in his progeny.' She said, 'Yes, then.'
So Allah, the Exalted, revealed at that time this verse: 'His mother bore him with aversion, and with aversion she gave birth to him.'
Because of the place of Jabra'il informing her of his killing, so she bore him with aversion because he would be killed, and she gave birth to him with aversion because he would be killed.
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet and Fatimah initially say they did not need the son who would be killed?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the pre-birth knowledge of Imam Husayn’s martyrdom, linking the physical burden of pregnancy to the spiritual weight of his future sacrifice. It underscores the Shia doctrine of *Nass* (designation), where the Prophet and Fatimah accept the Imamate's continuity in his progeny despite the sorrow of his death, a theme echoed in the Quranic description of Maryam's labor as 'unwillingly' or 'with distress' (41:15).

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. My father narrated to me from Sa’d ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥammād, from his brother Aḥmad ibn Ḥammād, from Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh, from his father, who said:

I heard Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) say: Jabra`īl came to the Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) and said, “Salām to you, O Muḥammad! Should I give you glad tidings of a son who will be killed by your nation after you?” The Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) replied, “I do not need such a son.” Jabra`īl ascended to the heavens and then came back to him again, repeating what he had said. The Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) replied, “I do not need such a son.” Jabra`īl ascended to the heavens (yet) again and then came back to him for the third time, repeating what he had said. The Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) replied, “I do not need such a son.” Jabra`īl said, “Verily your Lord has placed the succession in his progeny.” The Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) said, “Yes, (I accept).” Then the Prophet (s.a.a.w.) went to Fāťimah (s.a.) and said, “Jabra`īl came to me and gave me glad tidings of a son who will be killed by my nation after me.” Fāťimah (s.a.) replied, “I do not need such a son.” The Messenger of Allāh (s.a.a.w.) said to her, “Verily my Lord has placed the succession in his progeny.” Fāťimah (s.a.) replied, “In this case, yes (I will accept).”
Therefore, Allāh revealed this verse, “His mother bears him with aversion, and with aversion she gives birth to him” [46:15]

because Jabra`īl informed her that he would be killed. So “his mother bears him with aversion” because he would be killed. “And with aversion she gives birth to him” because (she knew) he would be killed.
